# ICP: Series A-C SaaS with a platform engineering team
*v2 — SaaS teams with 15+ engineers on call, buying after an outage customers noticed*

## Must-have
- B2B SaaS company at Series A to Series C (confidence: inferred; source: website)
- 15 or more engineers, with an on-call rotation (confidence: validated; source: founder, lost examples)
- Buyer: Head of Platform or VP Engineering holds the budget; below about 50 engineers, the CTO (confidence: validated; source: founder)

## Nice-to-have
- Already uses PagerDuty or Datadog (confidence: inferred; source: website)
- Reachable via: the platform engineering Slack community and SREcon speakers (confidence: validated; source: founder)
- Reachable via: LinkedIn (confidence: needs validation; source: founder)

## Disqualifiers
- Fewer than 15 engineers, or no on-call rotation (confidence: validated; source: founder, lost examples)

## Anti-ICP
- none yet

## Top pains (ranked)
1. Engineers lose hours writing incident postmortems by hand (confidence: inferred; source: website)

## Buying triggers
- Replacing a dedicated incident-management platform at renewal (confidence: needs validation; source: founder)
- An outage customers noticed, after which the CTO asks for better postmortems (confidence: validated; source: founder, won examples)
- Engineering passes about 30 people and on-call becomes a formal rotation (confidence: validated; source: founder)

## Changelog
- v1 (2026-10-23): first version, because of the website and a five-answer interview
- v2 (2026-10-23): removed the incident-platform disqualifier and added replacing one at renewal as a trigger, because the founder reported two wins last month from companies doing that
